You only get armor with the perk rune, but health and ammo drop occasionally regardless. Chainsaw kills fill all your ammo up regardless of what type of enemy you use it on, outside of the BFG and Chainsaw itself. It's also not a guaranteed one hit kill on everything, the smaller enemies you can run up and cut with impunity, but the bigger demons such as Mancubus and Barons of Hell you should to put a few rounds into them first or they'll sometimes block it and knock you back if you try to rush in with it. There is a chance they won't and you'll get the kill, but it doesn't always work. They don't have to be staggered like with a glory kill, but you do need to wear them down a little to get a guaranteed hit with the chainsaw.

Glory kills give you more health than a regular kill does, and every time instead of a random chance. The lower your health is, the better the chance of a health drop, and the more you get when it does happen with both a glory kill and a random drop. Killing something when you're close to dead almost always drops health. It might even be a 100% chance if you're really on the ropes, I'm not sure.

Ammo drops are much rarer, but tend to happen when your ammo is getting low. When it's really low it's actually pretty frequent. Between the pickups on the level and drops from monsters I rarely actually had to use the chainsaw and mostly finished the game using two weapons, the super shotgun and the gauss cannon. I very rarely had to switch to something else because I ran out of ammo. A couple of the bosses did that to me, and I did vary what weapons I was using for a while but that's basically it. At about the halfway point I started to basically exclusively use the Super Shotgun and Gauss Cannon right up until the final boss.

Super Shotgun is the best weapon in the game, especially after you get the double fire perk. The Gauss Cannon works really well for distant bigger enemies, such as Barons of Hell and Mancubus while they're still too far away for the Super Shotgun to do decent damage.

Also, you get more health by varying glory kills. Do the same one over and over and you get diminishing returns, but mix it up by coming in from different directions and you get more. How much is still based on how low your current health is, but it might drop two or three health bits with varying glory kills, where as doing the same one might only drop one.

It's a neat system that lends itself to a little strategy and rewards you for not doing the same thing over and over.

Basically all arena shooters do this though. You're supposed to be moving around the map as fast as possible, picking up health, armor, and possibly weapons. Even though the new Doom isn't really an arena shooter, it still has a few of the elements.

EDIT: I'm wrong about how similar it is to Serious Sam 3. Early on, it is a lot like that, but the further into the game you get, the less that's true. So, in my initial impression I wasn't wrong per say, but as the game progressed it really did turn out to be something different than it first seemed to me. Doom is it's own thing, not Serious Sam with prettier graphics. The game gets more and more vertically minded, and the smarter and more varied enemies are very different to fight. Sam's enemies are pretty much one trick ponies that either snipe at you or charge in head on, but Dooms baddies can vary and change tactics on the fly to respond to what you're doing.

After the first few levels, Doom is nothing like Sam 3 anymore, at least outside of a few gameplay mechanics being similar.

So, what is below here is true, but only for the first few levels. After that, the game becomes it's own thing with a few technical similarities, but a completely different feel and style of it's own. Some elements do remain similar, but not enough to really fairly compare them as heavily as I did.

It's Serious Sam 3 meets Brutal Doom.

The way enemies come in waves via teleporting, the way you trigger them by entering an area, the weapon mod secondary fire modes, and even the melee system are very similar to Sam 3. Not to mention the no cover, no auto heal, move and shoot and pick up health and ammo as you go kind of gameplay.

That's not really a bad thing as Serious Sam was meant to be a throwback to Doom [and Duke Nukem] to begin with. It works really well here, as while there are fewer enemies coming at you at once than Sam, they're smarter and tougher. Sam's enemies either charge right at you, or stand in one spot and shoot. Doom's baddies aren't going to pass a turing test, but try to flank you and will crawl around to keep their distance and get out of your line of fire while sniping you.

I've found that using the same tactics I use for playing Serious Sam 3 is the most effective way to play Doom 4. Dodge and shoot anything at a distance, melee anything that gets too close, and once everything is dead I scour the area for secrets and supplies before moving on to the next mob trigger. While that sounds obvious, I mean that the way I go about it is basically the same as it is when I play Sam. How I prioritize targets, the way I'm moving, my methodology is the same in a way that's different from most other shooters. It's a satisfying rhythm that I honestly think Doom does even better.

Also, you generally have less room to move around in than in Sam games, which usually give you a lot of open ground to maneuver in.

Doom is good, and scratches that old school itch. Originality is sometimes overrated anyway, especially considering that after Doom 3 fans asked for a throwback to the old Doom gameplay, and ID delivered exactly that with Doom 4. This is exactly what we asked for, and it's great.
